claims.text: A low-Al Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy with Al mole fraction around 0.1 is a disordered single-phase FCC alloy.
Increasing Al content beyond a critical threshold produces nanoscale ordered γ′-like precipitates in an FCC Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni matrix.
Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni undergoes a composition-dependent transition away from homogeneous disordered FCC as Al content increases.
The composition-dependent transition in the tested Al mole-fraction range is specifically an FCC-to-FCC-plus-γ′-like-precipitates transition rather than formation of BCC/A2 phases.
Higher Al content increases the driving force for short-range atomic ordering by changing the enthalpy–entropy balance.
The relatively large atomic size of Al can change lattice ordering and the relative stability of structural states in AlxCrCoFeNi.
Enhanced ordering nucleates stable nanoscale precipitates within the FCC matrix.
Atomic clustering or ordering governs phase stability in the Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni system.
Ordered γ′-strengthened FCC HEAs can exhibit thermal stability, coarsening resistance, and strength retention near 800 °C.
Formation of ordered precipitates in the quinary Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy will improve high-temperature strength relative to the low-Al baseline.
Formation of ordered precipitates will improve environmental resistance relative to the low-Al baseline.
Formation of ordered precipitates will improve radiation tolerance relative to the low-Al baseline.
Formation of ordered precipitates will improve cryogenic toughness relative to the low-Al baseline.
FCC-structured HEAs can possess high ductility and fracture toughness at ambient and cryogenic temperatures.
The controlled test varies Al mole fraction from approximately 0.1 to 0.5 while holding the relative Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni proportions and annealing conditions constant.
The hypothesis is bounded to Al mole fractions of approximately 0.1–0.5 and annealing at 900 K for 10 hours.
Failure to observe statistically significant ordered-precipitate formation or the anticipated property improvements relative to baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention and falsification design state that all samples receive the same 900 K/10 h anneal, whereas the conditions field describes the low-Al baseline as quenched from high temperature. This changes processing history as well as Al content and undermines the claimed composition-only comparison.
